slot.brief: A source and observer moving toward each other on a straight line; ask for the ratio of the apparent frequencies in approach and recede cases.

stem: A source of sound and an observer are moving toward each other along the same straight line, each with a speed of 20 m/s. If the speed of sound in still air is 340 m/s, the ratio of the apparent frequency heard by the observer when they approach each other to that when they recede from each other is
working:
Approach case (both moving towards each other):
$$f_{\text{app}} = f \frac{v + v_o}{v - v_s} = f \frac{340 + 20}{340 - 20} = f \frac{360}{320} = \frac{9}{8}f$$

Recede case (both moving away from each other):
$$f_{\text{rec}} = f \frac{v - v_o}{v + v_s} = f \frac{340 - 20}{340 + 20} = f \frac{320}{360} = \frac{8}{9}f$$

Ratio:
$$\frac{f_{\text{app}}}{f_{\text{rec}}} = \frac{9/8}{8/9} = \frac{81}{64}$$

Independent check: Approaching: fₐ/f = (340 + 20)/(340 − 20) = 9/8. Receding: fᵣ/f = (340 − 20)/(340 + 20) = 8/9. Thus fₐ/fᵣ = 81/64.
solution:
For Doppler effect, $f'=f\dfrac{v\pm v_o}{v\mp v_s}$, with signs chosen for approach or recession.
$$\frac{f_{\text{app}}}{f_{\text{rec}}}=\frac{(340+20)/(340-20)}{(340-20)/(340+20)}=\left(\frac{360}{320}\right)^2=\frac{81}{64}$$
